candidates.title: Fitting Regression Models with No Intercept Term
candidates.reason: Directly analyzes the theoretical and empirical consequences of omitting an intercept term in linear models, demonstrating how omitting the constant offset induces non-zero residual sums and systematic prediction bias.

candidates.title: Leverage and Regression Through the Origin
candidates.reason: Examines the geometric and diagnostic effects of suppressing the intercept parameter, illustrating how omitting an additive constant distorts leverage and residual distributions across finite observations.

candidates.title: Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Provides a dedicated pedagogical analysis in statistics education on intercept omission, detailing why residuals fail to sum to zero and how instructors should explain the resulting systematic offset.

candidates.title: Cautionary Note about R^2
candidates.reason: Demonstrates how standard goodness-of-fit metrics become invalid when an intercept is missing and residual means depart from zero, motivating careful separation of offset correction from evaluation metrics.

candidates.title: The Examination and Analysis of Residuals
candidates.reason: Foundational work establishing systematic residual analysis as a primary diagnostic tool to identify unmodeled structure such as uniform additive prediction offsets.

candidates.title: Graphs in Statistical Analysis
candidates.reason: Seminal educational paper establishing that aggregate summary statistics can conceal structural discrepancies, supporting the pedagogical need to directly inspect finite residual errors.

candidates.title: Residuals and Influence in Regression
candidates.reason: Classic diagnostic reference formalizing the properties of residuals, residual means, and model misspecification when fixed predictors lack necessary additive constants.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: Foundational methodology paper establishing the formal conceptual distinction between fitting a predictive adjustment on training data and assessing its validity on independent observations.

candidates.title: Estimating the Error Rate of a Prediction Rule: Improvement on Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Formalizes why evaluating a calibrated prediction rule on the identical finite dataset used to derive it produces an overly optimistic apparent error rate.

candidates.title: How Biased Is the Apparent Error Rate of a Prediction Rule?
candidates.reason: Analyzes the mathematical structure of resubstitution bias ('optimism'), explaining why assessing mean residual corrections on the same five observations systematically understates prediction error.

candidates.title: A Leisurely Look at the Bootstrap, the Jackknife, and Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: An influential tutorial explaining how data reuse during model evaluation creates unwarranted optimism, supporting the educational objective of demonstrating evaluation limits.

candidates.title: Neural Networks and the Bias/Variance Dilemma
candidates.reason: Provides foundational theory on the decomposition of prediction error into systematic specification bias and variance, formalizing the role of structural offset terms in finite-sample learning.

candidates.title: A General Framework for Forecast Verification
candidates.reason: Deconstructs predictive performance into separable attributes—specifically isolating systematic unconditional offset (calibration) from discrimination—supporting the conceptual separation of offset correction from evaluation protocol.
